title: Platform scales
prompt: A bench teaching model of the page 25 platform scales has a crate, three connected levers and a calibrated bar with a sliding weight. Load places a crate on the platform and unbalances the bar. Slide moves the weight until the three-lever system balances, then displays the mass reading. Add load adds a second crate and unbalances the bar. The user must Slide again before reading the increased mass. See-through shows first- and third-class levers, connecting bars, pivots, load path and sliding weight. Do not show an automatic spring or electronic reading.
blurb: A bench teaching model passes crate weight through three connected levers to a bar balanced by a sliding poise.

truthNotes: Three levers total, including the calibrated first-class bar. Two third-class stages have neutral travel ratios 3 and 4.
The load path is platform, stem, lever 1, connecting bar, lever 2, connecting bar, calibrated beam, poise.
A 1 kg poise at 20 cm balances one 20 kg specimen, and at 40 cm balances two. Readings are hidden during motion and whenever torque is not balanced.
The beam rises under added load while the existing poise position stays fixed. Slide represents manual adjustment. There is no spring or electronic transducer.
The base, cover, guides, supports, travel rest, colors and specimen staging are teaching fixtures. The isolated linkage is not an exact reconstruction of the page illustration.
Link lengths are maintained geometrically. Tare is idealized away; tilt is exaggerated and bounded. This is not a certified weighing instrument.
Force path overlays and specimens do not count as anatomy.
